disclaimer: Synthetic educational data created for NLP workshop purposes.
usage: Ground truth for dataset validation and analyzer evaluation only. Application analysis must extract questions, identify topics and compute frequencies from Markdown paper text independently; never load these labels or target frequencies as user-facing analysis.
counting_unit: One primary topic per top-level question slot; no sub-question double counting. Secondary related topics may be annotated but do not count toward these targets.

questions.question_text: Describe the encoder and decoder roles in a Transformer architecture, emphasizing how information passes between its main components.
Calculate IDF using ln(N/DF) for a term occurring in 2 of 8 documents, and explain what the resulting weight represents.
Explain how dense word representations differ from assigning each vocabulary item an unrelated one-hot coordinate.
Explain how self-attention assigns different relevance to tokens when constructing a contextual representation.
Compare stemming and lemmatization as text-normalization choices, using the forms 'study', 'studied' and 'studying' to illustrate the goal.
Calculate cosine similarity for vectors (1, 1, 0) and (1, 0, 1), showing the dot product and vector lengths.
Explain why positional information is needed in a Transformer when token representations are processed without a recurrent chain.
Explain how TF-IDF distinguishes a word frequent in one document from a word frequent throughout a collection.
Describe the mechanism that weights different token positions when forming a representation, rather than treating every context word as equally important.
Explain the distributional training idea of Word2Vec and how local context provides learning evidence.
Construct Bag of Words count vectors for 'students study language' and 'students study data' using one shared vocabulary.
Illustrate Continuous Bag of Words training with a short context window, identifying the surrounding-word input and the target word to predict.
Compare Transformer processing with recurrent processing in terms of token relationships and opportunities for parallel computation.
Compare raw term counts with term frequency inverse document frequency when ranking short course descriptions.
Discuss how distributional context can place related words near each other in a learned word-vector space.
Compare the two predictive directions used by Word2Vec while focusing on their common goal of learning word representations.
Analyze a text-cleaning plan that removes all short common words, explaining why preserving negation may matter for a language task.
Explain why comparing vector angles can reduce the effect of document length relative to comparing unnormalized dot products.
Illustrate the role of residual connections and feed-forward blocks in a Transformer layer.
Calculate TF-IDF for a term with raw term frequency 3, document frequency 2 and collection size 10, using TF multiplied by ln(N/DF).
Illustrate the roles of queries, keys and values in an attention mechanism for a short sequence.
Explain how BERT uses surrounding context to represent a token and why that differs from a static word vector.
Explain why a count-vector representation cannot distinguish 'students explain models' from 'models explain students' when their vocabularies match.
Illustrate Skip-Gram training by identifying how a target word is used to predict surrounding context words.
Discuss how an encoder-decoder Transformer connects an input sequence with an output sequence while retaining distinct component roles.
Discuss why a term present in every document receives zero IDF under the unsmoothed ln(N/DF) definition.
Compare a single static embedding for a word with its need for different meanings across sentence contexts.
Discuss why the choice of context window influences the relationships learned by a word2vec model.
Propose token boundaries for 'human-language methods in HCE-CSE603' and explain how handling hyphens changes the units represented.
Describe next-token prediction as a language-modeling objective and distinguish a likely continuation from a verified factual statement.
Analyze the architectural purpose of multiple representation layers in a Transformer without equating layer count with guaranteed accuracy.
Analyze how adding documents containing a previously rare term changes its inverse document frequency when that term becomes more prevalent.
Compare a single attention head with multi-head attention in terms of the relationships represented.
Describe masked language modeling in Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers and its connection to contextual learning.
List the bigrams in 'students study natural language' and explain what local order they retain compared with individual word counts.
Explain how two sentences with different vocabulary may express related meaning, and state why a numerical similarity score still needs interpretation.
Differentiate an encoder-only Transformer from an encoder-decoder arrangement in terms of how each uses the input representation.
Describe the role of term weighting in reducing the influence of common collection-wide words, using TF-IDF as the example.
Illustrate how word-vector geometry can express a relationship between vocabulary items, and state a limitation of interpreting closeness.
Describe how Word2Vec training differs from constructing a term-count vector directly from a document.
Differentiate word segmentation from merely splitting a string at spaces, using punctuation and a course code as examples.
Compare predicting a missing token from surrounding context with predicting the next token from preceding context as language-model objectives.
Describe how the Transformer model combines positional information with interactions among tokens to represent a sentence.
Describe why distributed representations share information across vocabulary items rather than treating every word as an independent symbolic index.
Analyze how relevance-weighted combinations of token information can relate distant positions without carrying context through every intervening step.
Discuss the encoder-oriented role of a BERT model without assuming that it is an unrestricted next-token text generator.
Compare unigram and trigram representations in terms of context retained and the number of possible observed sequences.
Describe meaning-based retrieval of a course description when the query uses a paraphrase rather than the course's exact title.
